module_title: Formative Assessment & The Holistic Progress Card (Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level explores the radical shift in how student performance is evaluated under NEP 2020. It breaks down the difference between Formative and Summative assessment and introduces the 360-Degree Holistic Progress Card (HPC) as the replacement for the traditional 'marks-sheet'.

core_concepts.title: Formative vs. Summative Assessment
core_concepts.description:
Examiners constantly test this distinction:
- Formative Assessment: Assessment *FOR* learning. It is continuous, ongoing, and diagnostic. It happens *during* the learning process (e.g., a quick quiz, observing a student reading) to give immediate feedback and improve teaching.
- Summative Assessment: Assessment *OF* learning. It happens at the *end* of a term or year (e.g., final board exams) to evaluate and grade the student.

core_concepts.title: The Paradigm Shift in NEP 2020
core_concepts.description: NEP 2020 mandates a complete shift away from high-stakes Summative assessments (which promote rote memorization and extreme stress) toward regular, competency-based Formative assessments (which promote critical thinking and continuous improvement).

core_concepts.title: What is the Holistic Progress Card (HPC)?
core_concepts.description:
The HPC is a revolutionary 360-degree, multidimensional report card that completely replaces the traditional marks-based report card.
- Traditional Report Card: Only showed cognitive (academic) marks out of 100.
- Holistic Progress Card: Shows a student's development across all domains: Cognitive (mind), Affective (emotions/values), and Psychomotor (physical/skills).

core_concepts.title: Assessment OF, FOR, and AS Learning
core_concepts.description:
1. Assessment OF Learning: The teacher gives a final exam to assign a grade (Summative).
2. Assessment FOR Learning: The teacher takes a class test to see what students didn't understand, so she can re-teach it tomorrow (Formative).
3. Assessment AS Learning: The student assesses *themselves* (Self-reflection) to monitor their own progress. The HPC makes Assessment *AS* learning mandatory.

important_entities.name: 360-Degree Evaluation
important_entities.key_fact: The core architectural change in the HPC.
important_entities.significance: In the old system, only the Teacher evaluated the student. In the 360-Degree HPC, evaluation is done by: 1) The Teacher, 2) The Peers (classmates), 3) The Student themselves (Self-Assessment), and 4) The Parents.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the HPC with the older Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE) introduced in 2009. While CCE was comprehensive, it was still heavily teacher-centric and often reduced to just 'more tests'. The HPC goes further by explicitly legally mandating **Self-Assessment** and **Peer-Assessment**, completely democratizing the evaluation process.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: OF = End, FOR = During, AS = Self
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Assessment **OF** learning is the final grade. Assessment **FOR** learning is the teacher adjusting the lesson. Assessment **AS** learning is the student judging their own work.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a CTET/KVS question asks 'What is the main objective of the Holistic Progress Card (HPC) proposed in NEP 2020?', ALWAYS select the option highlighting **'Multidimensional, 360-degree evaluation including self and peer assessment'**. Reject any option mentioning 'ranking' or 'comparing students'.
